However, even if that value were out of bounds, the memory it points to would not have been freed yet—the `m->ways` array is allocated as part of `m` and is freed only after the function completes. Therefore there is no use‑after‑free condition. The reported scenario would at most lead to an out‑of‑bounds read or a segmentation fault, but not a use‑after‑free. No other part of the code frees `m->ways` or `m->nodes` before this point, so the claim of use‑after‑free is unfounded.
